title: After fixing false-positive date warnings, do we still need a second AI model to verify every answer?
summary: Across 17 HIV chart scenarios (35 questions per setup), we compared four ways of running Google Gemma 4 12B: OpenMRS's built-in ChartSearchAI, Med Agent Hub's fast answer-only path, Med Agent Hub with deterministic chart and date checks, and a two-model setup that adds a separate Qwen 9B verifier model after every answer.
takeaway: Refining the deterministic date and chart checks eliminated false-positive warning banners and achieved zero unsafe answers and zero wrong dates across all three Med Agent Hub setups (79.0–81.1/100), compared with 70.6/100, 1 unsafe answer, and 3 wrong dates on built-in ChartSearchAI. Adding a second 9B AI verifier nudged the headline score by less than 1 point (81.1 vs. 80.4/100) at the cost of 27 extra seconds per question — showing fast deterministic checks do the real safety work.
